topic: The cost of hidden state under uniformly bounded stationary policy overlap. sampling: One stationary trajectory (X_t,A_t,Y_t)_{t=1}^T; joint state S_t=(X_t,H_t) has arbitrary finite state space, with no fixed bound on either cardinality; H_t never observed. All finite observed alphabets and known policies are supplied to the estimator; latent alphabet, transition/reward kernel and stationary distributions are unknown. This is a union of finite models; constants in the requested risk comparison must not depend on cardinalities. causal_kernel: A time-homogeneous joint kernel K(dy,dx_next,dh_next | x,h,a), as Hu–Wager Model 3. Under behavior, A_t is drawn from the known policy b(.|X_t), independently of all past and H_t conditional on X_t. Target e(.|X_t) is known, memoryless in the observed state. Rewards satisfy |Y_t|<=1. policy_overlap: For fixed zeta>0, e(a|x)<=exp(zeta)b(a|x) for all a,x (zero behavior cells therefore have zero target probability). Take a fixed binary action alphabet. Both policies may vary across instances and are revealed to the estimator. mixing: For fixed t0>0 and p in {b,e}, the induced joint-state kernel P_p satisfies ||nu P_p - nu_prime P_p||_TV <= exp(-1/t0)||nu-nu_prime||_TV for every pair of state distributions. Let d_b,d_e be their unique stationary joint-state laws; observed data start from d_b. latent_stationary_overlap: For a fixed C>1 independent of T and all state cardinalities, d_e(s)<=C d_b(s) at every joint state s=(x,h). This is a structural class restriction; neither d_b nor d_e nor their ratio is revealed. Do not replace it by overlap of observed X marginals. estimand: theta(K,e)=sum_s d_e(s) sum_a e(a|x) E_K[Y|s,a], the stationary mean outcome if target policy e were deployed. risk: R_T(t0,zeta,C)=inf over all measurable estimators based only on the observed trajectory and known (b,e,t0,zeta,C), sup over the displayed class, E[(theta_hat-theta)^2]. Supremum includes all finite state cardinalities and known-policy pairs obeying restrictions. Determine the exact asymptotic order of R_T(t0,zeta,C), with an explicit attaining observable-data estimator and a matching lower bound against all measurable estimators, for fixed positive t0,zeta and C>1. Characterize whether bounded latent stationary occupancy removes, reduces, or leaves unchanged the partial-observability penalty present in Hu–Wager. Rate and all boundary/logarithmic factors are outputs, not stipulated answers. All constants may depend on t0,zeta,C but not T or cardinality. A one-sided lower construction or a reuse of the unrestricted-class PHIW upper bound without matching the restricted-class converse does not deliver the kernel. No proxy informativeness, emission-rank, finite-memory, or known latent dynamics assumptions may be inserted. Consumer: Hu–Wager Section5.2 applies PHIW to the Luckett et al. (2019) mobile-health insulin-policy simulator calibrated to Maahs et al. (2012), with dietary intake hidden and ten-day hourly glucose trajectories. This result changes whether a substantive assurance that a candidate insulin policy stays within the logging policy's latent physiological occupancy can justify shorter history weights or faster precision, or whether collecting state/proxy information remains necessary. The paper-shaped deliverable must demonstrate that implication on a finite-state discretized version of this published application; it must not claim the original continuous simulator already satisfies the finite-state uniform contraction/overlap class. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A signed-depth reset chain keeps the same depth occupancy under both policies while treatment preserves a hidden sign and control erases it. Its target-to-behavior stationary ratios remain at most 1+epsilon, so epsilon can be fixed below C-1 independently of history length. A single noisy reward at terminal depth gives a target-value separation proportional to alpha^Q. The observed-filter argument uses the fact that terminal arrival forces the preceding Q rewards to be fair; a two-stage posterior bound suggests observed-path KL of order T alpha^(2Q) p^Q without revealing reset times. Balancing Q suggests the unchanged Hu-Wager risk exponent 2/(2+t0*zeta) for every fixed C>1, whereas C=1 permits parametric immediate weighting. Exhaustive small-path checks support normalization, occupancy and divergence scaling; a refreshed 360-state insulin-policy adaptation shows finite occupancy and nonzero immediate-weight bias. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the uniform terminal-posterior bound and chain-rule KL, including stationary pre-sample signs and every initial window. EARLY KILL TEST: Re-derive this observed-data KL bound before any formalization; a missing inverse-history factor or need to reveal resets invalidates the proposed lower construction. open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether the cardinality-uniform minimax MSE for stationary off-policy value estimation over finite POMDPs retains the Hu–Wager hidden-state rate under the fixed joint-state restriction d_e(s) ≤ C d_b(s) for every C > 1, or has a strictly faster exact order.

source_refs.claim: Proves the PHIW upper rate and a matching single-trajectory minimax lower bound under mixing and action overlap, but its depth-Q hard chain has d_e(h_Q)/d_b(h_Q) growing exponentially in Q and therefore does not establish the converse under fixed latent stationary overlap.
source_refs.author: Yuchen Hu and Stefan Wager

source_refs.claim: Shows that bounded or square-integrable stationary density ratios support root-T behavior in fully observed MDPs, whereas heavier ratio tails produce slower minimax rates.
source_refs.author: Mohammad Mehrabi and Stefan Wager

source_refs.claim: Shows in a finite-horizon POMDP framework that latent-state density-ratio coverage alone need not control observable future-dependent-value quantities, motivating separate outcome and belief coverage conditions.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Hu–Wager's upper bound remains valid on the restricted class, but their matching lower construction deliberately makes the target much more likely than behavior to reach the terminal hidden depth: the stationary ratio at that state grows exponentially with depth. Hence their converse does not survive d_e ≤ C d_b with cardinality-free C. Fully observed stationary-ratio estimators rely on observing the Markov state that supports the ratio, while the POMDP coverage literature shows that latent occupancy control alone need not control the observable inverse problem. The load-bearing unresolved step is therefore an observed-law lower pair inside the fixed-C class. The prompt's proposed signed-depth reset chain is only a hypothesis until its uniform terminal-posterior and chain-rule KL bounds include stationary pre-sample signs and every initial window without revealing reset times; any inverse-history loss would change the balanced rate. The repository's prior all-measurable OPE run independently flags the danger that a structured estimator comparison can hide alphabet-dependent rank or fiber constants.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A cardinality-uniform theorem giving an explicit observable-data estimator and the exact MSE order, including boundary or logarithmic factors, together with a matching Le Cam, Fano, or Bayes lower bound whose finite-state alternatives all satisfy d_e ≤ C d_b.

open_problems.why_unsolved: At C_T = 1, equality of the joint stationary laws makes the target value equal to a behavior-stationary expectation after the known one-step action correction, suggesting parametric MSE for bounded rewards under contraction. Neither Hu–Wager's unrestricted stationary-shift analysis nor fully observed density-ratio methods provides a uniform interpolation as δ_T ↓ 0. On the lower side, the first new step is to construct observationally close hidden-state alternatives whose stationary ratios remain within 1 + δ_T while tracking how value separation and observed KL jointly shrink; on the upper side, one needs a δ_T-sensitive bias envelope rather than the mixing-only PHIW bound. Prior CausalSmith overlap-frontier runs found exactly the relevant failure mode: estimator-side clipping envelopes did not yield shell-matched, class-uniform minimax converses.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A piecewise-sharp formula for R_T(t0,ζ,1+δ_T), with an observable hybrid estimator and matching local alternatives identifying the exact δ_T-dependent crossover between T^{-1} risk and the fixed-C hidden-state regime.

open_problems.why_unsolved: At the MSE-optimal PHIW depth, truncation bias is deliberately of stochastic order rather than negligible, and the selected depth grows with sample size. Hu–Wager's displayed CLT centers at the estimator's expectation, uses independent-unit variation, and itself cautions that the rate-optimal depth may violate its conditions; it therefore does not give uniform coverage for the true stationary value from the single trajectory considered here. Undersmoothing can make bias negligible only by exponentially inflating importance-weight variance, and the latent occupancy ratio is unavailable for an observable bias correction. The first proof step is a uniform asymptotic linearization or bias-aware concentration bound for the entire dependent PHIW depth process after selection. A prior reviewer independently identified selected-scale variance estimation plus a coverage theorem as the missing strengthening in a temporal-adaptation problem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit selected-history estimator and observable long-run variance or self-normalizer yielding uniform coverage with diameter of the square-root minimax-MSE order, together with a lower bound deciding whether honest adaptation requires an extra logarithmic or polynomial factor.

writing_exemplar.why: Its estimator-first account of partial-observability bias, variance, and Lepski depth selection provides the exact setup from which the unresolved coverage question emerges.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Partial histories restore consistent OPE -> optimal depth leaves truncation bias at the stochastic scale -> policy deployment requires uncertainty that stays valid after choosing that depth

open_problems.why_unsolved: The restriction concerns stationary laws on (X,H), but H, its cardinality, the controlled kernel, and both stationary laws are all hidden. Existing successful POMDP identification strategies turn latent structure into observable restrictions through decoupling, proxies, bridge equations, rank, or belief/outcome coverage; none is available here. Thus a substantive assurance of bounded latent physiological occupancy may change oracle minimax risk while having no empirically checkable implication. The first proof step is to construct or rule out two finite hidden-state realizations with the same law of (X,A,Y) under the known behavior policy but different truth values of d_e ≤ C d_b; a positive result would instead have to characterize the projection of this latent restriction onto observable finite-dimensional distributions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient observable-law characterization of compatibility with d_e ≤ C d_b, or an observational-equivalence theorem proving non-testability, supplemented in the testable case by a uniformly valid test.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames partial observability through failure of naive OPE and then isolates extra latent structure needed for recovery, matching an assumption-audit narrative.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Hidden state defeats observable OPE -> extra latent restrictions may restore guarantees -> determine whether the proposed stationary-occupancy assurance has any observable content

method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested resolution is an observational-equivalence frontier for a restriction on an unobserved POMDP state.

method_exemplars.technique: Use bridge-equation solvability as the successful comparator for translating latent quantities into observable moments, then determine whether occupancy boundedness alone implies any analogous moment restriction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a precise mechanism by which otherwise latent POMDP features become observable and therefore exposes what the overlap-only class lacks.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt multi-step observable-operator and rank arguments to delineate when longer observed pasts and futures reveal a latent restriction and when hidden refinements remain equivalent.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its spectral approach studies exactly how observed histories can reveal hidden-state structure, while making explicit the rank conditions forbidden in the target class.

literature_map:
Hu and Wager (2023, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:2110.12343) are the direct anchor: PHIW estimates stationary target value under sequential ignorability, geometric mixing, and action overlap, with a matching polynomial minimax rate.
Their lower chain reaches terminal hidden depth much more often under target than behavior, so its stationary ratio grows with depth; the focused scan found no published fixed-C joint latent-overlap converse.
Liu, Li, Tang, and Zhou (2018, NeurIPS, arXiv:1810.12429) avoid horizon products in fully observed infinite-horizon MDPs by estimating stationary state-density ratios.
Kallus and Uehara (2020, JMLR, arXiv:1908.08526) derive efficient doubly robust OPE from observed q-functions and marginalized density ratios.
Kallus and Uehara (2022, Operations Research, arXiv:1909.05850) show time-homogeneous observed Markov structure can break the horizon curse even with dependent trajectories.
Mehrabi and Wager (2025, arXiv:2402.08201) make stationary distributional overlap rate-driving in fully observed MDPs, but require access to the Markov state for ratio learning.
Tennenholtz, Shalit, and Mannor (2020, AAAI, arXiv:1909.03739) show generic partial observability can cause arbitrarily large OPE bias and use extra decoupling structure for recovery.
Bennett and Kallus (2024, Operations Research, arXiv:2110.15332) and Shi et al. (2022, ICML, arXiv:2111.06784) obtain identification and efficient or doubly robust estimation through bridge functions in confounded POMDPs.
Nair and Jiang (2021, arXiv:2109.10502) use spectral past/future proxies but retain rank, distinctness, and positivity requirements.
Miao, Qi, and Zhang (2022, NeurIPS, arXiv:2209.10064) give finite-sample POMDP OPE rates through sequential NPIV bridge estimation, with proxy informativeness and ill-posedness controlling rates.
Uehara et al. (2023, NeurIPS, arXiv:2207.13081) introduce future-dependent value functions; guarantees require histories and futures informative about latent state and Bellman completeness.
Zhang and Jiang (2024, NeurIPS, arXiv:2402.14703) show latent-state density-ratio coverage alone can leave exponential future-dependent-value quantities, motivating outcome and belief coverage.
Liao, Klasnja, and Murphy (2021, JASA, arXiv:1912.13088) provide long-run average-outcome confidence intervals in a fully observed mHealth MDP setting.
Hu–Wager Section 5.2 applies PHIW to a synthetic ten-day hourly glucose simulator following Luckett et al. (2019), with dietary intake hidden and calibration tied to Maahs et al. (2012).
That application motivates a finite-state discretized demonstration, but the original continuous simulator is not evidence for the requested finite-state uniform contraction and latent-occupancy class.
